grade_reason: Grade A. Two questions stood between this record and publication and both are now closed by evidence rather than by preference. The VAT ambiguity fell to arithmetic: ADDC published AED 7.84 and 10.41 in 2017, UAE VAT arrived on 1 January 2018, and TAQA Distribution's 2025 schedule publishes the same two figures unchanged — a rate that had absorbed the tax would have had to fall by 4.762%, and it did not move. The recurring-charge question needed an enumeration of a bill rather than a schedule of tariffs, and the publisher's own Understand Your Bill guide is one: it walks every section of a residential bill, and the water service line on its specimen equals the consumption section's total including VAT exactly, with no residual. Absence is established by what the bill contains, not by what the booklet omits.

reference_connection.designation: ADDC bands by residency class and dwelling type rather than by connection size: the Green allowance is 0.7 m³/day for an apartment and 5 m³/day for an expat villa. No connection-size parameter appears in the residential water tariff.

materiality.note: The two readings were 117.60 and 123.48 a month. The 2017 booklet and the 2025 booklet settle it: the rate is the same on both sides of the introduction of the tax, so it never contained it. 123.48 governs. This is the same species of argument as Dubai's per-gallon precedence — the arithmetic decides, not the prose.

component_states.basis: Resolved by an unchanged rate across the introduction of the tax. ADDC's Water & Electricity Tariffs 2017 gives expatriate residential water at 7.84 and 10.41; TAQA Distribution's Utility Tariff 2025, effective 1 January 2025, gives 7.84 and 10.41. UAE VAT began 1 January 2018, between them. Absorbing 5% into an unchanged headline would have required cutting the rate by 4.762%, and no cut occurred. The published rate is therefore net of VAT and the page footnote — charges will be inclusive of VAT at 5% — describes the amount billed. Neither booklet mentions VAT, which is what one expects of a schedule published before the tax and of one that states rates rather than bills.

Closed on 18 August 2026 by the publisher's residential Understand Your Bill guide, which is the enumeration Rule 7.6 asked for. Three things together: the guide walks every section a residential bill can carry and names the services it can charge for — Electricity, Water, Recycled Water, Municipality, with Waste Water and Waste among the activities an icon can show; the water consumption section of the specimen bill contains a Green band, a Red band, a total before VAT and VAT at 5%, and no fixed, standing, meter or service line anywhere; and the Water figure in Charges This Period is AED 261.75, which is exactly the consumption section's total including VAT. The last of these is the argument in arithmetic — a residual would be a recurring charge, and there is no residual. The two tariff schedules, which price no fixed charge for a metered residential account while pricing AED 150 a month for an unmetered one, corroborate it from the other side.
component_states.residual_caveat: The specimen bill is a UAE National account, the concessionary class §5.3 excludes, so it shows the format of a residential water bill and not the price of the benchmark one. What is being read from it is the enumeration, which is a property of the bill format rather than of the class; and the schedules price no fixed charge for either class. Recorded because it is the one seam in the argument, and a seam stated is worth more than a seam smoothed over.

component_states.question: TAQA Distribution's own Utility Tariff 2025 prices no wastewater tariff for any segment, and the publisher's bill guide names Waste Water among the activities a residential bill can show while giving no rate for it anywhere — and the specimen bill carries Recycled Water instead, which is a separate non-potable supply. Those facts are compatible only if the charge is levied by another body, or applies to some properties and not others. Until that is established, no Total Water Services figure is computed. The supply metric is unaffected: the guide's separate service lines are what show AED 7.84 to be water alone.
component_states.found_by: Rule 7.6, and it is the more consequential of the two: it decides whether a supply metric exists.

component_states.basis: The Utility Tariff 2025 states on its own face that it details the tariffs for the different customer segments as of 1 January 2025, and it is what the publisher's residential rates page links today as the full tariff guide. No 2026 document exists at the publisher. Under Rule 3.10 a live publisher schedule is the supersession check: a revised tariff would appear here, and does not.

The guide states VAT at the standard rate of 5% on water consumption charges and shows it computed on the period's net total: 249.29 × 1.05 = 261.7545, printed as 261.75 with VAT of 12.46. The rate was already established from the schedules; this is the billing side agreeing with the schedule side, which is what the capture queue asked this document to confirm.

The Green allowance is applied as the daily allowance multiplied by the days in the cycle. On the specimen — property type Flat, 30 days, 100 m3 — exactly 21.00 m3 falls in the Green band and 79.00 in the Red. 0.7 × 30 = 21. The band_basis_note recorded this as the Regulation and Supervision Bureau's stated construction; it is now the publisher's own arithmetic on a printed bill.

scope_disclosures: Reference customer is an expatriate in an apartment. Residency class and dwelling type both change the tariff, and neither is a property of the water.
The Green allowance is daily: 180 m³ a year is 0.492823 m³ a day against an allowance of 0.7, so the whole reference volume sits in the Green band with room to spare.
The figure is net rate plus 5% VAT: AED 117.60 of consumption and AED 5.88 of tax.
shape_note: A daily allowance, which is why the scenario has to become a daily rate before it meets a threshold. Applying the 0.7 m³ limit to a monthly volume of 15 m³ would put almost everything in the Red band and overstate the bill by more than 20%.

jurisdiction.note: City is a display layer. The observation belongs to jurisdiction x utility x service area x customer class x schedule x period.

band_basis_note: The Regulation and Supervision Bureau stated when the bands were introduced that the daily use determining the band is the average over the billing cycle — total use divided by the days in the cycle — and that exceeding the limit on a few days does not move the whole consumption to the red band. The TWJ scenario computes 180 / 365.2425 = 0.492823 m³/day, which is the same construction on an annual basis and lands inside the 0.7 green band either way. Recorded because the derivations differ even where the outcome does not: 15 m³ over a 30-day cycle is 0.5 m³/day, also green.

continuity.note: TAQA Distribution's Utility Tariff 2025, downloaded from the publisher on 18 August 2026 and linked from its residential rates page as the full tariff guide. The document dates itself to 1 January 2025 and the publisher has issued no 2026 edition. The schedule is the supersession check; a superseding rate would be published here. The capture queue still asks for an Executive Council or Department of Energy instrument, which would replace this basis with a recorded search over the instruments themselves.

public_reconciliation.limits: Every case is computed at the UAE National rates of AED 2.090 and 2.600, because that is the class of the only specimen bill the publisher prints. It reconciles the band mechanism, the VAT treatment and the absence of a fixed charge — the shape of the bill. It does not reconcile the benchmark figure of AED 123.48 a month, which is the same shape at the general class rates and which no publisher illustrates.

verbatim_check_note: The bill guide is a print-to-PDF and its specimen bill is reproduced as images inside the page, so its figures are not in the text layer and the extract carries the prose alone. No rate in this record rests on it: the rates come from the ADDC tariffs page, which is a text capture, and the guide is cited for an enumeration and a reconciliation rather than for a number.
